ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the cyclic pentagon $ABCDE$, if $\angle C + \angle CDE + \angle E + \angle EAB = 425^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle CDA$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since the sum of the interior angles of pentagon $ABCDE$ is $(5-2)\times 180^\circ=540^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle EAB+\angle B+\angle C+\angle CDE+\angle E=540^\circ$, \\
because $\angle EAB+\angle C+\angle CDE+\angle E=425^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle B=540^\circ-425^\circ=115^\circ$, \\
since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in circle $O$, \\
therefore $\angle B+\angle CDA=180^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle CDA=180^\circ-115^\circ=\boxed{65^\circ}$.

The problem statement gives ∠C + ∠CDE + ∠E + ∠EAB = 425°, that is, ∠BCD + (∠CDA + ∠ADE) + ∠AED + (∠EAD + ∠DAB) = 425°. Among them, ∠ADE + ∠AED + ∠EAD is the sum of the three interior angles of triangle ADE, equal to 180°. Also because the four points A, B, C, D are concyclic, quadrilateral ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, so the opposite angles ∠DAB + ∠BCD = 180°. Therefore the original sum is ∠CDA + 180° + 180° = ∠CDA + 360°. So ∠CDA + 360° = 425°, obtaining ∠CDA = 65°.
